meta.title: Finding Gold — How gold forms
meta.author: Ezekiel Minja
meta.description: Finding Gold: a field guide to mineral exploration. Educational — not a design standard.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Every gram of gold on Earth is older than the Earth itself.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: It was forged in dying stars, and in the collisions of their corpses. It arrived here in the dust that built this planet.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Most of it sank into the core. What we mine is the little that stayed behind in the crust. And it did not stay evenly.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Average crustal rock holds about four parts of gold per billion. To be worth mining, rock must be a thousand times richer than that. So something has to concentrate it.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Deep in the crust, water driven out of rock as it heats becomes a fluid at three to four hundred degrees, carrying silica, carbon dioxide and sulphur. Gold dissolves into it, bound to sulphur, at a few parts per billion.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Now give that fluid a road. In an old mountain belt the roads are faults and shear zones: fractures kilometres deep, where the crust has slipped past itself.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: The fluid rises. And as it rises, it loses pressure, it cools, and it reacts with the rock around it.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: So the gold complex breaks down. Gold drops out of solution. Into quartz, into carbonate, and into the iron sulphides the fluid builds on the way: pyrite, and arsenopyrite.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Repeat that ten thousand times across a million years, and you have a lode. A quartz vein, or a stack of them, threaded with metal.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: This is orogenic gold. It is why the great gold districts of the world sit in Archaean greenstone belts: the deformed roots of mountains two and a half billion years old.

dialogue.speaker: juma
dialogue.text: So if I find a quartz vein, I've found gold?

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: You've found a quartz vein. Almost all of them hold nothing.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Which is why exploration is a discipline. And why it begins with everything except digging.
